## The Rule

The owner’s rule: “If they are reported in order, then each one should be recorded as a
result, as long as each one is stronger than the last.
If a stronger result is reported first, then the other one should not be recorded since
it is weaker after that, unless there is some key reason it should be recorded.”

At each count the standing side starts at the record on `main`, frozen by `gather` in
[starts.yaml](starts.yaml) and never read from the working tree.
For n ≤ 324 it is the set of both upper lanes of the case record
(`packing/frontier/n-NNN.md`): each lane’s exact form where that is rational, a rigorous
90-digit interval where it is a closed form with square roots, an enclosure by exact
sign change of the root a `root(...)` form names, else its printed value within one unit
of its last place; with any register entry pending adoption that states a smaller bound,
and only the members nothing else is decidably below.
Above 324 it is the current beyond-horizon row of `frontier/source-coverage.yaml`, else
the grid ⌈√n⌉. The claims are then taken in the order they reached this repository:
issue, comment or pull-request creation, the update comment for a claim added to an
issue later, the commit for a claim added to a pull request later, and the first commit
for a publication in a watched repository that no issue reports.
A claim is recorded when every number it may be is below every number every member of
the standing side may be, and it becomes the standing side.
A claim equal to a member (a tie: the earlier holder keeps it) or above one is not
recorded, and the table names what holds the count.
A comparison the printed precision cannot decide is undecided; the undecided claim stays
beside the standing side until a claim is decidably below both.
Exact sides come from the lanes’ frozen claim records or, where `ledger.yaml` says so,
from the certificate at its pinned commit; this ledger compares sides and verifies no
certificate. Where a lane’s claim record or an exact decision’s receipt states how a
claim compares with a record lane or a pending register entry, that relation decides in
place of the prints while the record still prints what it read (`record_relations` in
`ledger.yaml`, each naming where it was read).
Sides are shown rounded up at 12 places where exact, as printed otherwise.

## Counts

arrangement), 0 refinements of a standing packing, 0 that no source classifies; 0
recorded by exception; 0 not recorded; 0 undecided.

A refinement is the same configuration with a tighter certificate (a padding reduction,
an exact-contact refinement, an exact attainment), as a source says; a new packing is
one its source says is new, including one a continued search found from another
arrangement.
The rule records both; the register credits a refinement as a regularization
of the packing it tightens.

### Publication in a Watched Repository

By default a certificate published in a watched repository, with no issue, competes as a
report from its first commit.
These are the counts where a verdict changes if such publications are not counted: each
publication drops out of the walk, and a later report may then be recorded in its place.
